t: This is Nottingham Place, a street in Westminster running from Marylebone Road in the north down to Paddington Street in the south. It takes its name from the Harley family estates in Nottinghamshire. The social reformer Octavia Hill once lived here and had a school on the street, and the stained glass artist Charles Eamer Kempe lived here too. Today the Maldives High Commission and the Latvian embassy are based here. Several people died on this street, among them two Royal Navy admirals, William Essington and Thomas Lennox Frederick, and the businessman Joseph Cyril Bamford, who founded the digger maker JCB.
